slides.page_title: The Producer Path: What Send Actually Does

items: `KafkaProducer` is thread-safe — one instance per app
`send()` returns `Future<RecordMetadata>`, no broker hit
Caller thread: serialize, partition, append to batch
Sender (I/O) thread: group by broker, write the socket

lines: // returns now; nothing on the wire yet

items: `RecordAccumulator`: deque of batches per TopicPartition
Pool sized by `buffer.memory`, default 32 MB
Serializers make `byte[]`; broker stores opaque bytes
Success gives topic, partition, offset, timestamp
Sticky fills one partition's batch, then switches
Bigger batches, lower latency, even long-run spread

slides.page_title: The Producer Path: What Send Actually Does (cont.)

items: `send(rec, (md, ex) -> ...)` — exactly one arg non-null
Callback runs on the Sender thread: never block in it
Slow work there stalls sends for every partition
`send().get()` is ~100x slower — batching collapses

blocks.title: Gotcha: the useless try/catch
blocks.text: A `try/catch` around `send()` catches only serialization and buffer-full errors. Broker-side failures never appear there — they arrive in the callback or the future.

a_bullets: `flush()` blocks until all buffered records complete

items: `acks` = how many replicas confirm before the broker replies
`acks=all` is the same value as `acks=-1`
Default `acks=all` since Kafka 3.0 with idempotence on
Older clients defaulted to `acks=1`

rows: loss only on full ISR loss

items: Pair it with `min.insync.replicas` or 'all ISR' means 'the leader'
`min.insync.replicas=2` with RF=3 is the standard safe triple
Tolerates one broker down, rejects writes at two down
ISR below minISR: broker throws `NotEnoughReplicasException`

blocks.title: An error beats silence
blocks.text: `NotEnoughReplicasException` reaches the producer, so a write that cannot be made durable fails loudly instead of vanishing.

items: `acks=all` waits for page cache, not `fsync` to disk
Durability here is replication, not flush
`unclean.leader.election.enable=true` silently defeats it
An out-of-sync replica becoming leader truncates acked writes
Throughput hit is far smaller than people assume
Batching amortizes the wait across many records
`acks=0` is incompatible with idempotence and transactions
The producer refuses to start with both configured
One batch = many records for one TopicPartition
Compressed and CRC'd as a single unit
`batch.size` (16384 B) is a byte cap, not a record count
A full batch ships at once, whatever `linger.ms` says
`linger.ms` (default 0): wait for more records before sending
`linger.ms=0` still batches while a request is in flight
Ships on whichever fires first: size full OR linger elapsed
Worst-case producer-side delay is about `linger.ms`
High throughput: `batch.size=32768..131072`, `linger.ms=5..100`
Bigger batches: more throughput, better ratio, fewer requests
A record over `batch.size` gets its own oversized batch
`max.request.size` (1 MB) caps one `ProduceRequest`

blocks.title: buffer.memory runs out
blocks.text: `buffer.memory` (32 MB) is the whole accumulator pool. When exhausted, `send()` blocks up to `max.block.ms` (60s), then throws `TimeoutException`.

items: Applied per batch, so bigger batches compress much better
Broker stores the compressed batch as-is; consumers decompress
Saves disk and network end to end
Broker `message.max.bytes` must be >= `max.request.size`

blocks.title: Gotcha: broker recompression
blocks.text: If the broker's `compression.type` differs from the producer's, it decompresses and recompresses every batch, burning broker CPU. Set the broker side to `producer`.

items: `batch-size-avg` — are batches actually filling up?
`records-per-request-avg` — amortization per round trip
`compression-rate-avg` — is the codec paying off?
`record-queue-time-avg` — accumulator backing up
`retries` defaults to `Integer.MAX_VALUE` in modern clients
The retry count is no longer the real bound — time is
`delivery.timeout.ms` (120s) is the true upper bound on `send()`
It covers batching, every retry and every in-flight attempt

blocks.title: Startup invariant
blocks.text: `delivery.timeout.ms >= linger.ms + request.timeout.ms`. The producer refuses to start otherwise, so a bad tuning attempt fails fast.

items: `max.block.ms` also bounds `partitionsFor()`
It is unrelated to the delivery timeout — different clock
`max.in.flight.requests.per.connection` (5) is per broker
Without idempotence, in-flight > 1 plus retries can reorder
Batch 2 succeeds while retried batch 1 lands after it
The old fix, `max.in.flight=1`, crushed throughput

blocks.title: Idempotence gives ordering back
blocks.text: With `enable.idempotence=true` ordering holds up to 5 in-flight requests, so you keep pipelining and lose nothing.

items: A retry after a lost ack duplicates — the at-least-once core
Delivery timeout gives `TimeoutException` with unknown outcome
The record may already sit in the log
Retry storms hold `buffer.memory` hostage and block producers
`enable.idempotence=true` — on by default since Kafka 3.0
Broker-side retries stop producing duplicates
Ordering survives up to 5 in-flight requests
Cost is near zero: leave it on
Producer gets a Producer ID via `InitProducerId` at startup
Issued by the transaction coordinator
Every batch carries (PID, epoch, base sequence)
Sequences increment per partition, per producer
Broker keeps the last 5 sequences per PID per partition
Held in memory and in the log's producer state snapshot
Already-committed sequence: acked again, never appended
Broker returns the original offset for the deduped batch
So the callback still sees a valid `RecordMetadata`
Out-of-order sequence: `OutOfOrderSequenceException`

blocks.title: The server enforces order
blocks.text: Sequence checking lives on the broker, not the client. That is exactly why `max.in.flight` up to 5 stays safe under retries.

items: Set automatically when idempotence is on
A conflicting explicit value throws `ConfigException`
Guarantees hold per partition, per producer session
A new instance gets a new PID and loses dedupe history
Epoch bump fences a zombie: older-epoch writes rejected
Idle too long and state expires: `UNKNOWN_PRODUCER_ID`

blocks.title: Not end-to-end exactly-once
blocks.text: Idempotence kills client retry duplicates only. An application-level re-send above the client still writes the record twice.

items: Extends idempotence to an atomic set of writes
Spans many partitions and many topics at once
Set `transactional.id` to a stable, unique per-instance string
That id survives restarts and is what enables fencing
`initTransactions()` fences any prior producer with that id
It bumps the epoch and aborts the old open transaction
Coordinator writes commit/abort markers into every touched partition
Reading transactional output requires opting in
LSO is the Last Stable Offset — the read ceiling
`read_committed` waits for the marker: extra end-to-end latency
`sendOffsetsToTransaction(offsets, groupMetadata)` joins the commit
The offset commit and the output writes land together
Exactly the mechanism behind `processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2`
`transaction.timeout.ms` (60s) <= broker max (default 15 min)
Otherwise `initTransactions()` fails at startup
Commit is a two-phase marker write — throughput cost is real
Batch many records per transaction, never commit per record

blocks.title: Fatal versus recoverable
blocks.text: `ProducerFencedException`, `OutOfOrderSequenceException` and authorization errors are fatal: close the producer. `KafkaException` on commit is ambiguous only for retriable causes, and `abortTransaction()` is the safe response to most failures.

items: At-most-once suits high-volume metrics only
At-least-once was the pre-0.11 default, still the pragmatic norm
Exactly-once needs `read_committed` consumers to close the loop
Idempotence covers one partition; transactions cover many
`acks=0`: loss is likely under any failure
`acks=1`: loss on leader failover
`all` + idempotence: loss only on total ISR loss
Exactly-once processing inside Kafka, not delivery outside it
An external DB sink still needs idempotent upserts
Or a dedupe key, or the transactional outbox pattern

blocks.title: The consumer decides too
blocks.text: Commit offsets before processing and you have at-most-once; commit after and you have at-least-once. Producer config alone does not set the semantics.

items: Dedupe on a business key or on (topic, partition, offset)
Store that marker with the write itself
A duplicate only hurts if the effect is not idempotent
'set balance to X' is safe; 'add X' is not

caption.text: Most Kafka data loss is not a broker problem — it is a `send()` whose return value nobody read. This handbook walks the whole producer path: the two threads behind one call, what each `acks` level really waits for, how `batch.size` and `linger.ms` race each other, and why `enable.idempotence=true` is free correctness. Ten pages of dense notes, config recipes and the invariants worth memorizing.
